title: Sampling strategy for the interactive image generator
prompt: Your text-to-image diffusion product lets users iterate on prompts in real time, then export a final hero image. How should you run the denoising/sampling pipeline to balance GPU spend, interactive latency, and output quality?
constraint: GPU cost and interactive latency are the binding constraints during iteration; users only need final-grade quality on the one image they keep, not on every draft.

options.why: Best per-image quality, but it spends premium GPU-seconds and adds seconds of latency to every draft the user discards. The constraint says iteration is cost- and latency-bound, so paying full price on throwaway drafts is exactly the waste to avoid.

Directly matches the constraint: cheap, low-latency previews keep iteration fast and GPU spend low, while full-step quality is reserved for the single exported image that actually needs it. You pay premium compute exactly once, where it matters.

Defensible — it nails the cost and latency targets across the board. But it caps final quality below what full sampling can reach, so the kept hero image is weaker than it needs to be; acceptable as a simpler pipeline, not the best fit since quality on the export is free to improve.

A middle setting that helps neither end: still slower and pricier than a distilled preview during iteration, yet visibly worse than full sampling on the export. It splits the difference instead of optimizing previews for the constraint and the final for quality.
